parts.latex:
Three years ago an appliance was valued at $\$2467$. Its value has depreciated by 15% each year, based on the declining-balance method.

What is its salvage value today, to the nearest dollar?

Peter currently earns $\$21.50$ per hour. His hourly wage will increase by 2.1% compounded each year for the next four years.

What will his hourly wage be after four years?

Suppose $a = \dfrac{b}{7}$, where $b = 22$.

What is the value of $a$, correct to three significant figures?

On a test, Zac’s mark corresponded to a $z$-score of 2. The test scores had a mean of 63 and a standard deviation of 8.

What was Zac’s actual mark on the test?

A student is thinking of a number. Let the number be $x$.

When the student subtracts 8 from this number and multiplies the result by 3, the answer is 2 more than $x$.

Which equation can be used to find $x$?
Which of the following best represents the graph of $y = 10(0.8)^x$?

There are 8 chocolates in a box. Three have peppermint centres (P) and five have caramel centres (C).

Kim randomly chooses a chocolate from the box and eats it. Sam then randomly chooses and eats one of the remaining chocolates.

A partially completed probability tree is shown.

\exfigure{38_q11_1}

What is the probability that Kim and Sam choose chocolates with different centres?

The time taken to clean a warehouse varies inversely with the number of cleaners employed.

It takes 8 cleaners 60 hours to clean a warehouse.

Working at the same rate, how many hours would it take 10 cleaners to clean the same warehouse?

parts.latex:
A total of 11 400 people entered a running race. The ratio of professional runners to amateurs was $3:16$. All the professional runners completed the race while 600 of the amateurs did not complete the race.

For those who completed the race, what is the ratio, in simplest form, of professional runners to amateurs?

The volume, $V$, of a sphere is given by the formula

$$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3,$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

A tank consists of the bottom half of a sphere of radius 2 metres, as shown.

\exfigure{38_q16_1}

Find the volume of the tank in cubic metres, correct to one decimal place.

The five-number summary of a dataset is given.

Lowest score $= 1$

Lower quartile $(Q_1) = 4$

Median $(Q_2) = 7$

Upper quartile $(Q_3) = 10$

Highest score $= 20$

Is 20 an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.

The fuel consumption for a car is 6.7 litres/100 km. On a road trip, the car travels a distance of 1560 km and the fuel cost is $\$1.45$ per litre.

What is the total fuel cost for this trip?

Adam purchased some office furniture five years ago. It depreciated by $\$2300$ each year based on the straight-line method of depreciation. The salvage value of the furniture is now $\$7500$.

Find the initial value of the office furniture.

City $A$ is in Sweden and is located at $(58^\circ\text{N}, 16^\circ\text{E})$. Sydney, in Australia, is located at $(33^\circ\text{S}, 151^\circ\text{E})$.

Robert lives in Sydney and needs to give an online presentation to his colleagues in City $A$ starting at 5:00 pm Thursday, local time in Sweden.

What time and day, in Sydney, should Robert start his presentation?

It is given that $15^\circ = 1$ hour time difference. Ignore daylight saving.

Julie invests $\$12\,500$ in a savings account. Interest is paid at a fixed monthly rate. At the end of each month, after the monthly interest is added, Julie makes a deposit of $\$500$.

Julie has created a spreadsheet to show the activity in her savings account. The details for the first 6 months are shown.

\extable{38_q21_t1}

By finding the monthly rate of interest, complete the final row above for the 7th month.

The table shows the income tax rates for the 2020–2021 financial year.

\extable{38_q22_t1}

William has a gross annual salary of $\$84\,000$. He has allowable tax deductions of $\$900$ for home-office equipment and $\$474$ for union fees. William must also pay a Medicare Levy of 2% of his taxable income.

Calculate the total tax payable by William including the Medicare Levy.

Nina plans to invest $\$35\,000$ for 1 year. She is offered two different investment options.

Option $A$: Interest is paid at 6% per annum compounded monthly.

Option $B$: Interest is paid at $r$% per annum simple interest.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the value of $r$ in Option $B$ that would give Nina the same future value after 1 year as for Option $A$. Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.stem_latex:
For a sample of 17 inland towns in Australia, the height above sea level, $x$ (metres), and the average maximum daily temperature, $y$ ($^\circ$C), were recorded.

The graph shows the data as well as a regression line.

\exfigure{38_q33_1}

The equation of the regression line is $y = 29.2 - 0.011x$.

The correlation coefficient is $r = -0.494$.

parts.label: i
parts.latex: By using the equation of the regression line, predict the average maximum daily temperature, in degrees Celsius, for a town that is 540 m above sea level. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

parts.label: ii
parts.latex: The gradient of the regression line is $-0.011$. Interpret the value of this gradient in the given context.

parts.label: b
parts.latex:

The equation of the regression line is $y = 45.6 - 0.683x$.

The correlation coefficient is $r = -0.897$.

Another inland town in Australia is 540 m above sea level. Its latitude is 28 degrees south.

Which measurement, height above sea level or latitude, would be better to use to predict this town’s average maximum daily temperature? Give a reason for your answer.

questions.stem_latex:
A publisher sells a book for $\$10$. At this price, 5000 copies of the book will be sold and the revenue raised will be $5000 \times 10 = \$50\,000$.

The publisher is considering increasing the price of the book. For every dollar the price of the book is increased, the publisher will sell 50 fewer copies of the book.

If the publisher charges $(10 + x)$ dollars for each book, a quadratic model for the revenue raised, $R$, from selling the books is

$$R = -50x^2 + 4500x + 50\,000.$$

A graph of this quadratic model for revenue is shown. A dashed line is used for values of $x$ which are not relevant to the practical context of this problem.

\exfigure{38_q35_1}

parts.label: a
parts.latex: By first finding a suitable value of $x$, find the price the publisher should charge for each book to maximise the revenue raised from sales of the book.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the value of the intercept of the parabola with the vertical axis.

notes: 2021 NESA HSC Mathematics Standard 2. Section I Q1-15 (15 marks), Section II Q16-41 (85 marks); numbering continuous as printed. No answer key or marking guidelines in this file, so no is_correct / solutions. Q23 and Q24 parts share a stem so kept together. Q33 has sub-parts a(i), a(ii) stored as leaf parts with parent a, and b. Q1 and Q14 carry a printed 'NOT TO SCALE' (Q1 in text, Q14 inside the figure crop). Answer lines, extra writing pages, booklet covers and the reference sheet are skipped. Blank axes (Q24c), answer grid (Q34) and unlabelled normal curve (Q41) are cropped as figures. Content is in the Mathematics Standard 2 syllabus (some Q3, Q17, Q28, Q33 statistics/bivariate items are Standard course content: MST-11-08 / MST-12-S1-06, not Advanced); no typos found in the paper.
